chapters.title: Chapter 651: An Unexpected Survivor
paragraphs: "So if this place really is a prison, we’re trapped right in the middle of it."
Lian gave a faint smile.
"Apparently."
"And we don’t even know where the exit is."
"That’s why we’re looking for it."
Rindo sighed, but before their conversation could continue, another change occurred in their surroundings.
The wind stopped.
The golden leaves of the trees near the road remained still, and the Withered passing through the arch turned their heads toward the sky almost at the same time.
Lian immediately noticed the change in the mana flow.
It’s time.
Two also raised its head.
A low, deep growl came from the wolf’s throat, and its ears moved backward.
"The Fourth Judgment?" Rindo tightened his grip on his spear.
The young Vorhelm looked at the black pupil of the sun.
"Yeah."
A few moments later, the Judge’s huge voice spread across the entire land.
"The Fourth Judgment has begun."
The golden rings began to rotate.
The sunlight became stronger for a moment, and thin threads of light spread through the different layers of the air.

Lian immediately recognized the identification stage, the same flow he had seen during the Second Judgment, but this time, for the first time, he was standing very close to one of the ancient structures.
He focused all his attention on the energy paths, the threads of light passed over the Withered, and some creatures fell to their knees while others tried to hide behind the pillars.
But the light continued moving without being stopped by the obstacles.
Finally, one of the threads stopped on the same Withered that had asked for help a few minutes earlier.
The creature raised its head.
A ring of golden light formed around its body, and the Judge’s voice was heard again.
"The condemned has been identified."
The Withered tried to move backward, but its feet were stuck to the ground against its will.
"First Charge: Violation of a Previous Judgment."
Lian looked at Rindo for a moment.
The same charge as Sareven.
"Second Charge: Leaving the Designated Area."
The creature placed its hands on its head.
The Judge’s voice continued without any change.
"Third Charge: Disobedience of the State of Stillness."
The Withered looked toward the stone arch for a moment, then lowered its head.
"I... came back..."
But those words did not change the judgment.
"Sentence: Execution."
The golden light became stronger.
Lian observed the connection paths with [True Sequence], the energy threads connected to the creature’s body and soul.
Then deeper structures began to form.
The Withered tried to move its body one last time, but before it could take a step, light spread from inside its body.
A few moments later, the creature disappeared without leaving a trace.
Rindo lowered his gaze for a moment, he still had not gotten used to the sun’s executions, and he probably never would.
But Lian continued looking at the place where the execution had happened, because right after the process ended, a familiar flow had appeared.
Part of the golden energy moved toward the ground.
That same flow.
This time, unlike before, he was in a good position to observe it.
He followed the energy threads, they passed through the stone surface of the road and then moved toward the ancient arch, entering one of the mana lines carved into its base.
He narrowed his eyes.
’So they really are connected.’
The golden energy moved along the stone paths for several seconds, then passed through the white roots and traveled into the depths of the ground.
But this time, he managed to follow part of its path farther than before, the energy flow passed beneath the arch and moved in a direction that led toward the center of the land.
Finally, it disappeared into depths beyond the range of his senses.
Lian remained still for several seconds.
Rindo noticed his expression.
"What did you find?"
Lian pointed toward the base of the arch.
"Part of the energy from the judgment passed through this structure."
"Where did it go? Were you able to see?"
"Toward the depths, but its path continued toward the center."
"So these structures really are connected to the Judgments." Rindo looked at the lines carved into the stone for a moment.
Lian nodded.
"At least some of them, but I still don’t know why the energy is being transferred." He placed his hand on the surface of the arch.
Mana was still flowing inside the stone, but the judgment energy was no longer passing through it, as if the structure had returned to its normal state after completing its task.
He looked at the sun for a moment.
’If I can find out where this energy is going...’
Perhaps he could better understand the connection between the Judgments, the Withered, and the collapse of the land.
But it was still too early to reach a conclusion.
Golden beams had also appeared in other areas.
The sun had identified several more condemned creatures, and the sound of their sentences being announced could be heard from far away.
Lian and Rindo remained beside the arch for a while until the sun’s rings finally began to slow down.
"The Fourth Judgment has been completed."
There was silence for several seconds, and then the same familiar sentence was heard.
"Next Judgment: In twenty-four hours."
The golden light around the condemned disappeared, the wind began flowing between the broken pillars again, and the remaining Withered continued moving as if nothing had happened.
Lian slowly breathed out.
Another day.
Only one day remained until the next Judgment.
And considering how the condition of the land was getting worse every day, he could not be sure how much of the ground would remain intact by then.
He recorded the location of the arch and the path of the energy flow, then looked at Rindo.
"We need to move."
Rindo glanced at the sun.
"I hope we finally find some proper answers there."
Lian gave a faint smile.
"Me too."
After some time, both of them climbed onto Two’s back again.
The huge wolf passed along the ancient road and reached an area where parts of the ground were covered with broken stone pillars.
In the distance, the red light of molten rock could be seen through the cracks, but unlike the areas behind them, most of the rocky platforms in this section were still intact.
Two crossed between them with long jumps.
Lian was also examining the information he had obtained from the stone arch.
He now had three important pieces of information.
The Withered were moving toward the center against their own will.
Parts of the underground structures were connected to the Judgment system.
And the energy remaining after the executions was being transferred into the depths through these same structures, at least in some places.
But he still did not know what was waiting at the end of those paths, whatever is down there, it’s probably worth seeing.
At that moment, Two slowed down.
Lian raised his head, the huge wolf had stopped on one of the rocky platforms.
Its ears had turned toward an area among the broken pillars, and its gaze remained fixed on one point.
The young Vorhelm placed his hand on its neck.
"Did you find something?"
The wolf gave a short growl and then turned its head toward a narrow path between the pillars.
Rindo also noticed the change in the wolf’s behavior, and he adjusted the spear in his hands.
"Is there something over there?"
Lian did not answer, because at that moment, the sound of a heavy impact came from the distance.
BAAANG!
Several pieces of stone broke away from one of the broken pillars, and then the body of a Withered was thrown out of the dust.
The creature’s body rolled across the ground and struck a stone wall, and a few moments later, it stopped moving.
"Someone’s fighting." Rindo narrowed his eyes.
Lian nodded, he had also detected the mana flows from the battle, but the strange thing was that one of the flows belonged to an Awakened.
Not a Withered.
He signaled Two for a moment, and the huge wolf remained silently on the platform.
Both young men slowly climbed down from its back, farther away, several Withered were moving around a human figure.
One of the creatures rushed toward that figure, but before it could get close, it received a heavy strike and fell to the ground.
The second creature attacked from the opposite direction.
This time, the young man standing between the pillars quickly changed his position and struck the Withered’s body.
BOOM!
The creature’s body was thrown several meters backward, and then the man slowly began moving.
Lian narrowed his eyes for a moment.
Those movements...
Something about that person’s fighting style was familiar.
But there was still a long distance between them, and part of the man’s body was hidden behind the broken pillars.
"Lian..." Rindo had apparently noticed the similarity too, in fact, he was also somewhat happy that they had found another living Awakened.
At least they were finally sure they were not alone.
The young Vorhelm raised his hand slightly.
Rindo fell silent.
At that moment, the unknown man passed beside one of the pillars.
His armor was damaged, and parts of it were covered with dirt and dark stains, but the main structure of his clothing was still recognizable.
The man took a few more steps and then stopped in an unusual way, he slowly raised his head and looked at the Hollow Sun.
For several seconds, he did not move at all, he paid no attention to the Withered around him or the stones collapsing near his feet.
Then he lowered his head and started walking again.
They continued staring at him.
But just as the man stepped out from beneath the shadow of the pillar, the golden sunlight fell on his face.
This time, there was no doubt.
Lian knew that face, the same person they had received no new reports about since entering the Land of First Dawn.
"That’s... Roderick." Rindo slowly breathed out.

chapters.title: Chapter 652: The Arrogant Tyrant
paragraphs: Roderick Ashen.
Lian looked at the young man standing among the broken pillars for several seconds.
It had not been long since their last meeting, but Roderick’s appearance had changed.
Part of his armor was damaged, dried bloodstains could be seen on his right sleeve, and several deep scratches covered his forearm.
Even so, he still had the same arrogant way of standing.
His shoulders were pulled back, his chin was slightly raised, and his gaze made it seem as if he expected every creature around him to move aside before he reached them.
A few steps away from him, the body of a Withered was lying on the ground.
But contrary to what one might expect, Roderick was not even looking at the body.
His head was raised, and he was looking directly at the Hollow Sun.
Rindo stood beside him and raised his spear slightly.
"We finally found him."
"Yeah." Lian nodded.
"But something’s strange."
He looked at his friend for a moment.
Rindo pointed toward Roderick.
"Since we saw him, he’s stopped in the middle of moving several times, even when that Withered attacked him, it was like he needed a few seconds to react."
Lian had noticed this too, even so, he could not tell the reason from his current distance.
Perhaps Roderick was extremely tired, perhaps he was injured, or maybe something else had happened to him over the past few days.
I’d better talk to him first.
Lian placed his hand on Two’s neck.
The Eight-Disaster Wolf remained on the rocky platform after receiving his command, its ears were turned toward Roderick, but it still showed no signs of wanting to attack.
Then he took a few steps forward.
"Roderick."
His voice spread between the broken pillars.
The young man lowered his head, his gaze remained fixed on Lian for a moment, but contrary to expectations, he did not react immediately.
Several seconds passed.
Then the corner of his mouth rose.
"Vorhelm."
Roderick opened and closed his right hand, and dried blood fell from his fingers.
"So you finally made it here too."
Lian raised an eyebrow slightly.
"What a warm welcome, I didn’t think you’d missed me this much."
"You still have that annoying mouth." Roderick gave a short laugh.
"And you still have that same arrogant face."
There was silence for a moment.
Roderick turned his gaze away from Lian and looked at Rindo.
"The Student Council President is here too? I thought you two had separated."
Rindo did not lower his spear.
"We’ve been together since the first day, where have you been? We haven’t received any reports from you for days."
The young Ashen shrugged.
"I’ve been busy hunting, this place had more treasures than I expected."
Then he looked toward the broken plain.
"At least until that damn thing woke up."
He pointed at the sun with his chin.
"Since the exit was sealed, most of the paths have disappeared too, I’ve tried several times to return to the outer area, but every time, a new crack blocked my path."
Rindo looked at Lian for a moment.
Roderick apparently knew nothing about the situation at the central base.
Lian had not expected otherwise, he had entered the inner areas alone on the first day and had never returned to Alaric’s emergency base.
"So you still don’t know what happened outside." Lian said.
Roderick raised an eyebrow.
"What do you mean?"
"An emergency base was established near the entrance, most of the Association’s forces and several of the Chosen had gathered there."
"And?"
"It doesn’t exist anymore, the entire area is covered in molten rock."
Roderick’s smile faded, and his gaze remained on Lian for several seconds.
"Did everyone die?"
"We don’t know, when I returned, I couldn’t find anyone."
Roderick only nodded, but unlike Rindo, he did not ask any more questions about the people at the base.
He did not know them, and apparently, in the current situation, the fate of the Association’s forces did not matter much to him.
Instead, his gaze fell on Lian’s level, and he paused for a moment.
"Level 31?" From the boy’s presence, he could more or less tell his level.
He stared at him for several seconds and then laughed.
"I really have to admit that your growth speed is abnormal, Vorhelm, you were only Level 23 during our last battle."
"I killed a few monsters." Lian shrugged.
"A few?"
"Enough to reach Level 31."
Roderick smiled, but something in his gaze had changed, he still remembered their last battle very clearly.
The Shattered Crown Examination.
The place where, despite having a sixteen-level advantage and using the first trait of his Class Tree, he had failed to defeat Lian.
But what remained in his mind even more than the result of the examination was the way the spectators had looked at him.
The professors, guild representatives, and students who had watched Level 39 Roderick use all his strength, only to end up with a draw against a Level 23 Awakened.
For someone who had always considered himself worthy of the title of King, that result was nothing less than humiliation.
He slowly clenched his fingers.
"Even so, you’re still behind me."
"In terms of level? Yeah." Lian looked at him.
"In every way."
Vorhelm remained silent for a moment and then gave a faint smile.
"Then apparently, you didn’t learn much from our previous fight."
Roderick’s smile disappeared.
For several seconds, only the sound of molten rock flowing through the distant cracks could be heard.
Roderick tilted his head slightly.
"You know, you’ve always had this problem since high school."
"What problem?" Lian raised an eyebrow.
"You couldn’t accept your place." His voice was calm, but the familiar contempt could be heard in it.
"Even when you’d lost everything, you still acted like you were better than everyone else."
Lian looked at him for a moment, and old memories returned to his mind.
The days when the members of the Vorhelm Family had changed the way they looked at him after his failed awakening.
The time when Elena ended their relationship, and some time later, when even the house where he had grown up no longer had a place for him.
During that same period, Roderick had obtained his Four-Star Class and joined one of the Twelve Ancient Guilds.
The difference in their positions had become so large that many people who had previously known Lian preferred to stay away from him.
Roderick had also taken advantage of that opportunity.
But now?
Lian no longer needed to prove anything to his past, he tilted his head slightly.
"Are you done?"
"What?" Roderick frowned.
"I thought you were giving a speech about the past, I just wanted to know if I had to listen until the end."
For a moment, a muscle beside Roderick’s eye moved, this lack of concern bothered him more than a direct insult.
Because Lian had not even become angry.
It was as if everything Roderick had once done to ruin his life was no longer worth discussing.
"Very well." He took a step forward. "Then we’d better test it again."
Rindo narrowed his eyes and added.
"Roderick, now isn’t the time for this, the land is falling apart and—"
"I’m not talking to you." Roderick’s tone became sharper, and then he looked directly at Lian.
"This time, there’s no crown, no clock, and no excuse to retreat, just you and me."
Lian looked at the surrounding cracks for a moment.
"You really want to fight here? Are you crazy?" He felt that something was wrong with this boy’s brain.
Of course, his instincts were actually telling him that Roderick was not in his normal state, and even his behavior showed some signs of it.
Had something happened to him?
"Are you scared?"
"No. I was just wondering what you’ll blame this time if you lose again." The young Vorhelm let out a short sigh.
Roderick no longer smiled, and mana began flowing along his arms.
"Then let’s find out."
"Move back a little." Lian looked at Rindo.
His friend hesitated for a moment.
But then he moved toward a higher rocky platform to the north.
Lian turned to face Roderick again, the distance between them was nearly twenty meters.
He did not know why this idiot wanted to fight under such circumstances, but he was not going to refuse either.
"Well, start."
Roderick did not wait any longer, and mana moved from his spine toward his legs and joints.
[Tyrant’s Advance]
He took the first step.
BOOM!
The stone beneath his foot broke.
With the second step, his body’s speed increased, and with the third step, he had almost completely closed the remaining distance.
His right fist moved toward Lian’s face, but he raised his left hand.
CRACK!
Their forearms collided, but this time, unlike their previous battle, Lian did not even move backward, and the force of the strike spread through his body.
Roderick noticed the difference, but he had no time to think, because Lian’s right fist immediately moved toward his chest.
Roderick brought his other arm forward.
[King’s Reprisal]
A short stream of golden energy moved from his forearm toward his shoulder and chest.
This skill stored part of the force from an incoming strike inside his body’s structure and allowed him to return it with his next counterattack.
But when the young Vorhelm’s fist struck, he noticed something.
BAAANG!
The pressure of the strike was much greater than he had expected, his right foot slid several centimeters backward across the stone, and the mana stored in his arm shook violently.
What?
How the hell has this bastard become so much stronger since our last meeting?
He has even gone through his Second Evolution... but why does he seem weaker in terms of raw power?
"What? Were you expecting less?" Lian gave a faint smile.

"We don’t know, when I returned, I couldn’t find anyone."
Roderick only nodded, but unlike Rindo, he did not ask any more questions about the people at the base.
He did not know them, and apparently, in the current situation, the fate of the Association’s forces did not matter much to him.
Instead, his gaze fell on Lian’s level, and he paused for a moment.
"Level 31?" From the boy’s presence, he could more or less tell his level.
He stared at him for several seconds and then laughed.
"I really have to admit that your growth speed is abnormal, Vorhelm, you were only Level 23 during our last battle."
"I killed a few monsters." Lian shrugged.
"A few?"
"Enough to reach Level 31."
Roderick smiled, but something in his gaze had changed, he still remembered their last battle very clearly.
The Shattered Crown Examination.
The place where, despite having a sixteen-level advantage and using the first trait of his Class Tree, he had failed to defeat Lian.
But what remained in his mind even more than the result of the examination was the way the spectators had looked at him.
The professors, guild representatives, and students who had watched Level 39 Roderick use all his strength, only to end up with a draw against a Level 23 Awakened.
For someone who had always considered himself worthy of the title of King, that result was nothing less than humiliation.
He slowly clenched his fingers.
"Even so, you’re still behind me."
"In terms of level?
Yeah." Lian looked at him.
"In every way."
Vorhelm remained silent for a moment and then gave a faint smile.
"Then apparently, you didn’t learn much from our previous fight."
Roderick’s smile disappeared.
For several seconds, only the sound of molten rock flowing through the distant cracks could be heard.
Roderick tilted his head slightly.
"You know, you’ve always had this problem since high school."
"What problem?" Lian raised an eyebrow.
"You couldn’t accept your place." His voice was calm, but the familiar contempt could be heard in it.
"Even when you’d lost everything, you still acted like you were better than everyone else."
Lian looked at him for a moment, and old memories returned to his mind.
The days when the members of the Vorhelm Family had changed the way they looked at him after his failed awakening.
The time when Elena ended their relationship, and some time later, when even the house where he had grown up no longer had a place for him.
During that same period, Roderick had obtained his Four-Star Class and joined one of the Twelve Ancient Guilds.
The difference in their positions had become so large that many people who had previously known Lian preferred to stay away from him.
Roderick had also taken advantage of that opportunity.
But now?
Lian no longer needed to prove anything to his past, he tilted his head slightly.
"Are you done?"
"What?" Roderick frowned.
"I thought you were giving a speech about the past, I just wanted to know if I had to listen until the end."
For a moment, a muscle beside Roderick’s eye moved, this lack of concern bothered him more than a direct insult.
Because Lian had not even become angry.
It was as if everything Roderick had once done to ruin his life was no longer worth discussing.
"Very well." He took a step forward.
"Then we’d better test it again."
Rindo narrowed his eyes and added.
"Roderick, now isn’t the time for this, the land is falling apart and—"
"I’m not talking to you." Roderick’s tone became sharper, and then he looked directly at Lian.
"This time, there’s no crown, no clock, and no excuse to retreat, just you and me."
Lian looked at the surrounding cracks for a moment.
"You really want to fight here?
Are you crazy?" He felt that something was wrong with this boy’s brain.
Of course, his instincts were actually telling him that Roderick was not in his normal state, and even his behavior showed some signs of it.
Had something happened to him?
"Are you scared?"
"No.
I was just wondering what you’ll blame this time if you lose again." The young Vorhelm let out a short sigh.
Roderick no longer smiled, and mana began flowing along his arms.
"Then let’s find out."
"Move back a little." Lian looked at Rindo.
His friend hesitated for a moment.
But then he moved toward a higher rocky platform to the north.
Lian turned to face Roderick again, the distance between them was nearly twenty meters.
He did not know why this idiot wanted to fight under such circumstances, but he was not going to refuse either.
"Well, start."
Roderick did not wait any longer, and mana moved from his spine toward his legs and joints.
[Tyrant’s Advance]
He took the first step.
BOOM!
The stone beneath his foot broke.
With the second step, his body’s speed increased, and with the third step, he had almost completely closed the remaining distance.
His right fist moved toward Lian’s face, but he raised his left hand.
CRACK!
Their forearms collided, but this time, unlike their previous battle, Lian did not even move backward, and the force of the strike spread through his body.
Roderick noticed the difference, but he had no time to think, because Lian’s right fist immediately moved toward his chest.
Roderick brought his other arm forward.
[King’s Reprisal]
A short stream of golden energy moved from his forearm toward his shoulder and chest.
This skill stored part of the force from an incoming strike inside his body’s structure and allowed him to return it with his next counterattack.
But when the young Vorhelm’s fist struck, he noticed something.
BAAANG!
The pressure of the strike was much greater than he had expected, his right foot slid several centimeters backward across the stone, and the mana stored in his arm shook violently.
What?
How the hell has this bastard become so much stronger since our last meeting?
He has even gone through his Second Evolution... but why does he seem weaker in terms of raw power?
"What?
Were you expecting less?" Lian gave a faint smile.

paragraphs: Roderick threw another punch without answering, this time from a lower angle.
Lian moved out of its path with a short movement, but Roderick immediately turned his elbow and sent it toward his side.
[Tyrant Body]
Roderick’s body structure strengthened the main joints and bones of his body with mana, which was why even his elbows, knees, and shoulders could be used as powerful weapons.
The young Vorhelm placed his forearm in front of the elbow.
The second collision happened.
Then the young Ashen raised his right knee, but this time, Lian moved first and placed his palm on his shoulder, changing the knee’s direction with a short push.
At that same moment, his left fist struck his opponent’s side.
BOOM!
Roderick moved several meters backward, the soles of his shoes slid across the stone surface, and he finally regained his balance.
He looked at Lian for several seconds.
How much has his strength increased?
In their last battle, he had managed to land heavy strikes on Lian using the stored power of King’s Reprisal and his own Class ability.
But now, even their normal clashes were difficult to compare.
"Do you still want to continue?" Lian lowered his hand.
Roderick clenched his teeth.
"Shut up."
Then he attacked again, this time, his steps were shorter, he did not intend to repeat the same mistake from their previous battle.
He remembered how Lian had broken the chain of Tyrant’s Advance by changing the slope of the icy ground.
So while moving, he sent part of his mana into the ground to detect any changes before placing his foot down.
But this time, Lian did not use ice and took a small treasure out of his storage space.
[Core of the Fallen Star]
This S-Rank treasure, which he had obtained at the southern spring, allowed him to change gravity within specific areas.
Its power depended on the amount of mana consumed, and changing gravity over large areas required much more energy.
But right now, he only intended to affect a small area.
Roderick took his second step, and just as he was shifting his body weight for the third step, the gravity beneath his right foot increased.
Not enough to pin him to the ground, but just enough to change the way his body weight shifted for a moment.
But that small change was enough.
His chain of movements was disrupted, his right shoulder lowered slightly, and part of his gathered momentum was lost.
Lian moved, and his right fist struck his side.
BAAANG!
The young Ashen was thrown several meters to the left, but before falling, he struck the ground with his palm and turned his body.
He landed on one knee.
He let out a short breath and then fixed his gaze on the young Vorhelm.
"What did you do?"
"I just made you a little heavier and lighter." Lian shrugged.
Roderick frowned.
He knew very well that Lian had previously possessed the ability to control ice, but he had never felt such a change in the force acting on his own body.
A new skill?
But he still did not know where it came from, and Lian had no intention of explaining further.
Roderick stood up again, this time, before moving, he shifted his weight between his feet several times.
Then he moved forward with shorter steps, he was trying to maintain his balance even if gravity changed.
Lian noticed the adjustment in his movements.
’He’s still the same Roderick, at least he learns from his mistakes.’
When the distance became shorter, Roderick stopped advancing and moved directly into close combat, sending his right fist toward Lian’s face.
Vorhelm moved out of its path, but his enemy immediately changed the punch into an elbow strike.
Lian raised his forearm, and the collision happened, and at that same moment, dense mana formed behind Roderick’s other fist.
[Crushing Decree]
Lian remembered the skill.
The first strike transferred compressed mana to the target’s surface, and a moment later, a second explosion occurred from that same point.
This time, he had no intention of taking it directly.
His palm struck Roderick’s wrist and changed the punch’s direction by several centimeters, the strike passed beside Lian’s body and hit the stone pillar behind him.
CRACK!
For a moment, nothing important happened.
Then...BOOOOM!
The middle section of the pillar broke from within, and broken stones fell onto the road.
Roderick was still preparing to launch his next attack, but Lian had already moved, and his left fist went toward his chest.
The young Ashen raised his forearm.
[King’s Reprisal]
But just as he received the strike, a gray figure appeared along the path of Lian’s previous punch.
Roderick narrowed his eyes.
What?
The gray figure repeated the same movement.
BOOM!
The second strike hit Roderick’s forearm, forcing him to stop his counterattack halfway.
But it was not over yet, another gray figure formed along the same path, and a moment later, the third punch landed.
BAAANG!
This time, Roderick’s defense opened, and Lian used the opportunity to drive his right knee into his stomach.
His body bent backward, he took several unsteady steps, and finally managed to remain standing.
Lian lowered his hand.
[Funeral of the Nameless]

This new skill created up to two gray figures from the path of a single attack, the figures were not independent beings; they only repeated the same attack after a short delay, with power depending on the amount of mana consumed.
Because of this, even after defending against the first strike, Roderick still had to consider the paths of the following attacks.
Roderick looked at Lian for several seconds, a thin line of blood ran down from the corner of his mouth, and he wiped it away with the back of his hand.
"Another trick?"
"Didn’t you like it?" Lian smiled.
Roderick did not answer, but something in his gaze had changed, he was no longer only trying to defeat Lian.
He wanted to understand how the same young man whom no one had once considered important could now stand against him with such calmness.
And worst of all, why did Lian still not seem to be taking the battle seriously even after receiving several heavy strikes?
He took a deep breath and then clenched his fingers.
"I thought I wouldn’t have to use this anymore."
"Oh? You still have something left?" The young Vorhelm raised an eyebrow.
Roderick raised his gaze.
"I’m no longer the same Roderick from the Shattered Crown Examination.
And at that moment, the mana flow around his body changed, at first, a faint light appeared along his arms and shoulders.
Then the normal color of mana slowly disappeared and was replaced by white and golden light.
A heavy pressure formed in the surroundings, and small stones around his feet began to shake, even the air near his body changed for a moment.
Lian narrowed his eyes.
Ascended Mana?
Ascended Mana was a stage above normal mana that Awakened could reach after their Second Evolution.
Its nature was still mana, but its quality was much higher, which was why using it could increase the power of normal skills several times.
He had seen this energy before, when he had returned to the Vorhelm Family for his sister’s birthday celebration and fought with his older brother.
The first time he had seen Ascended Mana was during his battle with Cassius.
But Roderick was Level 40, and if he had truly managed to bring his mana to this stage, the meaning was clear, he really had completed his Second Evolution.
Roderick raised his right fist, and white and golden light gathered around his knuckles.
"This time, you’ll understand the real difference."
Lian looked at the energy around his body for a moment and then gave a faint smile.
"How nice, then you won’t have any excuses left."
The young Ashen said nothing this time and simply placed his right foot forward.
[Imperial Edict: Kneel]
A heavy pressure settled over the area.
Small stones were pressed against the ground, and the mana around Roderick became denser.
Lian felt greater resistance against his body when he moved; it was as if the area near Roderick had been filled with heavy layers of energy.
This skill did not control the opponent’s mind.
By releasing dense mana into an area around himself, Roderick made it harder for his enemy to move and change direction.
Farther away, Rindo, who was standing on the northern platform, was forced to lean on his spear for a moment.
"What is this?"
Two let out a low growl and took several steps back.
But the young Vorhelm simply took one step forward, and the pressure beneath his feet increased.
He activated [Core of the Fallen Star].
Gravity changed in a small area around his body, reducing part of the heaviness that made it difficult for him to move.
Of course, Roderick’s pressure did not completely disappear, because not all of it came from gravity, but this much was enough.
He took his second step.
Roderick frowned.
"How—"
"Did you think I’d actually kneel just because you told me to?"
Lian closed the distance and sent his right fist toward Roderick, but this time, his enemy did not retreat.
White and golden mana flowed along his body, and by turning his shoulder, he changed the direction of the strike.
Then he moved forward with a quick movement.
[Thronebreaker Sequence]
The first impact came from his shoulder, and a heavy force struck Lian’s chest, before he could counterattack, Roderick’s elbow came down from a higher angle.
Lian raised his forearm.
CRACK!
The strike was redirected, but this was exactly the reaction Roderick had wanted from the beginning, and by turning his body, he sent the final punch upward toward the open part of Lian’s defense.

chapters.title: Chapter 654: Even Ascended Mana Isn’t Enough ( Bonus )
paragraphs: Thronebreaker Sequence was a three-stage skill that gradually opened the opponent’s defense with a shoulder strike, an elbow strike, and a final punch.
And now, Roderick had strengthened all these movements with Ascended Mana.
For a moment, Lian realized that he no longer had enough time to completely redirect the punch, so he lowered his left arm.
The collision happened.
BOOOOM!
The force of the strike passed through his forearm and pushed him several meters backward, the stone beneath his feet cracked, but Roderick gave him no time.
With [Tyrant’s Advance], he closed the distance again and threw another punch.
This time, Lian moved out of its path, but Roderick’s Ascended Mana had increased the speed of his attacks, and the next punch struck the young Vorhelm’s shoulder.
Then another strike came from the right.
Lian blocked both of them, but he noticed that Roderick was now much faster than he had been a few minutes earlier.
Well, things have finally become a little serious.
He decided to examine the paths of the attacks for a moment.
[True Sequence]
The mana flows became clearer.
He noticed that his enemy was consuming a considerable amount of mana to maintain the pressure field and strengthen his attacks.
And more importantly, when performing Thronebreaker Sequence, most of the energy moved from his right shoulder to his elbow and then to his fist.
’So if I interrupt the second movement, the third won’t have its full power.’
Roderick approached again, and their shoulders collided, but this time, Lian did not retreat.
Instead, he took half a step to the left and allowed the pressure to pass beside his body.
The young Ashen’s elbow rose, but before it could reach him, Lian grabbed his wrist, and at that same moment, the gravity beneath his opponent’s feet changed.
Roderick’s body became heavier for a fraction of a second.
The young Vorhelm used that opportunity, and in a fraction of a second, a huge ice claw covered his fist.
[Glacial Reaper Claw]
And his right fist struck Roderick’s stomach.
BAAANG!
He bent backward, but before he could fully regain his balance, another strike from Lian hit his face, and this time, Roderick could not completely block it.
His body was thrown several meters backward and rolled across the stones, and for several seconds, only the sound of his heavy breathing could be heard.
Then he placed his hand on the ground and slowly stood up, blood was running down from the corner of his mouth.
But what bothered him even more than the pain was Lian’s gaze.
Vorhelm was not even breathing heavily, as if this entire battle had only been an opportunity to test a few new skills.
Why?
Roderick clenched his teeth.
I’ve completed my Second Evolution.
I have Ascended Mana.
I have an evolved Four-Star Class.
Then why can’t I defeat him?
He thought about Lian’s level for a moment.
Thirty-one.
Only Level 31.
Once, this difference had been enough to make him feel that even fighting Lian was an insult to his position.
But now?
He had been forced to use Ascended Mana and his main skills, and he still had not achieved anything.
"Roderick, a piece of advice." Lian looked at him.
The young Ashen raised his head.
"What?"
"You’d better pay some attention to the condition of the ground before you use up all your mana."
Roderick frowned for a moment and then noticed the shaking beneath his feet, the cracks created by their previous strikes were slowly spreading.
But before either of them could move, the sound of breaking stone came from the depths.
CRAAAACK!
A large part of the western platform broke away, and the ground between them split open, while a huge column of hot steam rose into the air.
Lian immediately opened his wings, and at the same time, Two jumped from the northern platform and carried Rindo away from the collapsing area.
Roderick also used Ascended Mana to jump across the crack, but this time, instead of landing on the same platform as before, he landed on a more distant part of the southern path.
For a few moments, all three of them looked at each other from a great distance.
Then another shaking began.
This time, it was stronger, and the ancient pillars broke one after another, while part of the road fell into the cliff.
"I think our fight is over for now." Lian looked at Roderick.
"It’s not over yet, Vorhelm!" Roderick answered in a rough voice.
"Then I hope you don’t get buried under the rocks before next time." The young Vorhelm shrugged.
Then he moved his wings and flew toward Rindo’s platform.

Roderick watched his path for a moment, his fists were still clenched, but he could not cross the huge crack that was growing wider every moment, especially after consuming a considerable amount of mana.
He finally lowered his gaze, the blood on his knuckles had dried, and for several seconds, an image of their old battle appeared in his mind.
Lian at Level 23.
Himself at Level 39.
And a result he had never been able to forget.
Now he was Level 40, and he had also completed his Second Evolution.
But the result? Once again, that same feeling of humiliation.
He slowly breathed out, and then a faint sound came from the depths of the crack.
He turned his head, for a moment, his gaze remained fixed on the darkness below, and without even realizing it, he took a step toward the edge.
It was as if something down there was calling him.
But just before taking a second step, he shook his head.
"What am I doing?" He whispered in disbelief.
He looked at the crack for several seconds, then frowned and moved away from it.
Deep underground, something remained silent.
When Lian reached the northern platform, Rindo had already climbed down from Two’s back.
He was looking at the new crack from a short distance away; a crack that had divided their previous path into two completely separate sections.
"Did you really have to fight each other right here?" Rindo asked as Lian approached.
"I just wanted to talk to him."
"And the result was the road splitting in half?
"Well, the second part was the ground’s fault, anyway, Roderick isn’t exactly in his right mind."
Rindo looked at him for a moment and then sighed, but he had also realized that something was wrong with Roderick.
Even so, they were not in a position to do anything about it.
Lian looked toward the horizon for a moment.
The ground was still shaking farther away, and red steam was rising from the cracks.
The paths used by the Withered had also become more crowded compared to the previous day.
The closer they got to the center, the more mutated creatures they saw moving toward the same area from different directions.
"We need to gather as much information as possible before the next Judgment." He said quietly.
Rindo looked at him.
"You still want to get closer to the center?"
"Yeah. But through another route."
Vorhelm pointed toward the huge crack between them and their previous path.
"We don’t have a way back for now, so we’d better make use of the time we have left."
Rindo thought for several seconds and then nodded.
"Alright."

paragraphs: But just as Two turned toward a platform in the east, the ground beneath the path ahead of them split open.
CRAAAACK!
A large part of the plain collapsed, and ancient stone pillars along with huge white roots appeared from beneath the ground. More groups of Withered also emerged from the new cracks.
Some were between Level 35 and Level 40, but there were also larger creatures among them that were nearly four meters tall and were climbing up the walls with their mutated limbs.
Rindo prepared his Ten Star Spear.
"Lian, I don’t think we can get through here without fighting."
Lian looked around.
To the north, several rocky platforms were still intact, but the western paths had collapsed, and a large group of Withered was approaching them from the south.
"Apparently not." He climbed down from the Eight-Disaster Wolf’s back. "Two, take Rindo to the northern platform. I’ll clear the path."
The huge wolf jumped across the crack with a long leap and landed on the northern platform with Rindo.
At that moment, a Level 45 Withered attacked Lian from the left.
[Frost Dominion]
Cold spread across the ground, and the creature’s legs became trapped in ice. The Withered tried to free itself, but Lian reached it before it could succeed.
BAAANG!
His fist destroyed the creature’s head.
[You have killed a Level 45 Withered.]
Two more attackers approached from the right, but Lian simply turned his hand.
[Glacial Reaper Claw]
A huge claw made of solid ice formed in the air and passed through the first creature’s body. The second tried to retreat, but the claw changed direction and blocked its escape path.
[You have killed a Level 37 Withered.]
[You have killed a Level 41 Withered.]
Lian looked toward the northern platform.

Two had pushed several attackers back with its huge paws, while Rindo used his spear from the wolf’s back to stop the weaker creatures from getting closer. When two Level 40 Withered approached them, the wolf entered the battle itself.
They’re fine for now.
But another shaking occurred in the ground.
Several cracks connected to each other, and dozens of new Withered began climbing out through the hot steam.
"This is getting ridiculous."
Lian held out his hand.
[Core of the Fallen Star Activated]
Mana flowed into the Core of the Fallen Star and changed the gravity acting on several huge stones.
The falling stones slowed down in the air for a moment. Then, as the direction of gravity changed, they moved toward the path the Withered were using to climb out.
BOOOOM!
Several large stones struck the wall and blocked the attackers’ main path.
Lian had no intention of closing the entire crack; doing so would consume a lot of mana and would probably become useless again after the next shaking.
But just as he was about to move toward Rindo, the sound of a heavy impact came from the west.
BAAANG!
A huge Withered was thrown backward from among the rocks and struck a broken pillar.
Lian turned his head.
Roderick Ashen appeared from the dust.
His battle armor was damaged, and white and golden mana was still moving around his right arm, but something about his appearance had changed.
His hair was messy, blood had dried on his chin, and his fingers kept opening and closing. His shoulders sometimes tightened without his control, but his gaze did not leave Lian even for a moment.
"Vorhelm..."
Then the corners of his mouth rose.
"Ha... hahaha..."
Lian frowned.
What the hell is wrong with him now?
Roderick lowered his head, but his laughter became louder.
"Finally... I finally found you!"
And he attacked without the slightest warning.
[Tyrant’s Advance]
BOOM!
With three steps in a row, he closed the distance of several dozen meters and threw his right fist toward Lian’s face.
The young Vorhelm moved his head a few centimeters to the side. The fist passed beside his cheek, but Roderick immediately followed with another attack using his elbow and knee.
CRACK!
Lian blocked the strikes and answered with a direct punch to Roderick’s chest.
BAAANG!
The young Ashen moved several meters backward.
But he did not even stop to regain his balance.
"Hahaha! That’s it!"
Despite the blood coming from the corner of his mouth, he ran toward Lian again.

This behavior was different from the Roderick Lian knew. He had always been an intelligent fighter who could adapt and examine his opponent’s tactics, but now he did not even care about getting injured.
He only attacked.
A Level 47 Withered approached him from behind, but without turning his head, Roderick struck the creature’s face with his elbow and immediately turned toward Lian again.
"Vorhelm!"
Lian caught his next punch.
"Roderick, can you hear yourself?"
"Haha... shut up!"
The young Ashen even tried to strike his face with his forehead.
Lian moved backward and created some distance again with a short punch to his stomach.
But Roderick continued laughing.
This doesn’t even look like his fighting style anymore.
Before Lian could decide how to stop him, a deep shaking came from the east.
The Withered near one of the cracks suddenly stopped moving. Some even tried to retreat against the force pulling them toward the center.
Lian glanced in that direction.
What’s happening?
Green steam rose from the depths and reached one of the rocks.
The stone surface began to corrode.
After activating [True Sequence], Lian observed thin mana flows inside the steam that were entering the structures of objects.
Poison?
At that moment, Roderick attacked him again.
"Look at me, Vorhelm!"
Lian redirected the punch and pushed the young Ashen several meters backward with a strike to his shoulder.
Roderick lost his balance, and his other fist struck a rock.
The stone broke.
But when he saw the blood on his fingers, he only laughed louder.
"Hahaha! Good... very good!"
Lian narrowed his eyes.
He’s really going crazy.
At the same time, a Level 47 Withered entered the steam.
The skin on its legs turned dark, and the tissues of its body began to break down. The creature tried to retreat, but its muscles tightened, and it fell to the ground.
Then an armored hand appeared from the crack.
A moment later, a tall figure wearing black, worn armor climbed up from the depths and landed on the rocky platform with a controlled movement.
Steam of different colors came out from the gaps in its armor, and two glowing eyes examined the surroundings from behind its twisted face.
A window appeared before Lian.
[Nine-Venom Castellan]
[Race: The Withered]
[Rank: Unholy]
[Level: 25]
An Unholy?
The Nine-Venom Castellan was only Level 25, but its Unholy Rank showed that its body structure and abilities were very different from those of ordinary monsters.
Lian looked at the steam around the creature.
So this is what made the others run away.
The Castellan raised its right hand.
Green steam moved directly toward the fallen Withered and covered its body.
A muffled sound came from the creature’s throat.
Then its skin, muscles, and bones began to break down almost at the same time.
In less than one second, nothing remained of the Withered.
But the steam did not spread away.
Dark green threads returned from the place where the creature had been destroyed toward the Castellan and entered the gaps in its armor.
With [True Sequence], Lian noticed that these threads contained part of the Withered’s life force.
The old cracks in the Castellan’s armor closed, the light in its eyes became stronger, and the mana pressure around it increased.
It absorbed its life energy?
It seemed that after breaking down the victim’s body, the Castellan could use part of its life force to recover and strengthen itself.
On a battlefield with hundreds of Withered, such an ability could be extremely dangerous.
The Castellan raised its head.
Its gaze passed over the surrounding Withered, moved past Rindo and Two, and did not even stop on Roderick, who was still laughing.
Finally, its glowing eyes became fixed on Lian.
The young Vorhelm gave a faint smile.
"What an interesting creature."
But the Castellan showed no reaction.
It simply raised its right hand.
Green steam moved directly toward Lian.
Not toward Rindo or even Roderick and for sure not the Withered that were only a few meters away from it.
Only Lian.
Oh? So you’ve chosen me?
The young Vorhelm moved out of the steam’s path, but the Castellan changed the direction of its hand, and the poisonous stream followed his new path.
Lian moved behind one of the broken pillars.
The steam struck the pillar, and the stone surface began to break down within a few moments.
Then another stream of steam came out from the Castellan’s left hand.
This one was dark purple.
By examining the mana flow, Lian noticed that the green poison mainly destroyed the body and defensive structures, while the purple poison could disrupt the target’s mana flow.
And both were moving directly toward him.
At that moment, loud laughter came from behind him.
"Hahahahaha!"
Lian turned his head.
Roderick was standing with his head lowered. His eyes had turned red, and an unnatural smile could be seen on his blood-covered face.
"Even the monsters want to kill you, Vorhelm!"
Then he laughed louder.
"Hahaha! But no!"
He clenched his fingers.
"You’re mine!"
Lian paused for a moment.
What?
Roderick charged toward him with a loud roar.
[Tyrant’s Advance]
This time, he did not even try to stay away from the poisonous steam.
He ran directly through a thin part of the poison, and the protective layer of Ascended Mana around his leg began to weaken.
But his laughter did not stop.
"Hahaha!"
His fist moved toward Lian’s face.
The young Vorhelm moved out of the strike’s path, but the Nine-Venom Castellan also sent another stream of steam toward his new position at the same time.
Damn it.
Lian opened his [Wings of God] and lifted himself off the ground.
The poison passed beneath his feet and broke down the stone surface.
But Roderick did not retreat even in this situation. Using Ascended Mana, he launched himself into the air and sent another punch toward Lian.
"Come back!"
Lian raised his forearm.
CRACK!
The two strikes collided.
Then, with a short turn, the young Vorhelm moved away from Roderick and kicked him in the chest.
BAAANG!
Roderick was thrown toward the ground but even while falling, he was laughing loudly.
Lian remained in the air for several seconds and moved his gaze between the two enemies.
On one side was Roderick, who seemed to have lost all his instinct for self-preservation and only wanted to attack him.

On the other side stood an Unholy creature that could break down its enemies’ bodies with poison and absorb part of their life force; a creature that had chosen no target other than Lian since the moment it appeared.
And around them, hundreds of Withered were moving across the collapsing ground.
Lian let out a short sigh.
This situation isn’t good at all.

Lian remained in the air for several seconds and moved his gaze between the two enemies.
On one side was Roderick, who seemed to have lost all his instinct for self-preservation and only wanted to attack him.

On the other side stood an Unholy creature that could break down its enemies’ bodies with poison and absorb part of their life force; a creature that had chosen no target other than Lian since the moment it appeared.
And around them, hundreds of Withered were moving across the collapsing ground.
Lian let out a short sigh.
This situation isn’t good at all.

chapters.title: Chapter 656: A Land of Blood and Poison
paragraphs: Lian remained in the sky for several seconds.

A little farther away, the Nine-Venom Castellan stood motionless, and its gaze did not leave the young Vorhelm even for a moment.
But now that some of the steam around the Castellan had spread away, Lian could see its appearance more clearly.
The creature was nearly four meters tall.
The black armor covering its body did not look much like armor made by humans; its plates had grown directly from its body, and streams of dark liquid moved between them.
Its shoulders were covered with long, curved blades, and a worn cloak hung behind them.
A cloak that seemed to have once belonged to an ancient ruler, but now only kept the remains of its former glory.
Even so, the most frightening part of its appearance was its head.
Nine black, curved blades extended from the back of its skull and formed an uneven crown, and between every two blades, there was a small opening from which steam of a different color came out.
Its face was hidden behind a white, bone-like covering, a deep crack extended from its forehead to its chin, and several rows of thin, dark teeth could be seen through the opening.
But its two eyes... the Castellan’s eyes were nothing like those of a mindless creature.
They were calm.
Focused.
And they followed Lian’s movements with such patience that it seemed the creature was already examining the best way to kill him.
Lian used [True Sequence] to examine the mana structure around the Castellan.
Nine independent streams moved inside the creature’s body, and each of them was connected to one of the crown’s blades and carried different energy to its limbs.
These streams were the source of its nine types of poison; poisons that were not only different in color, but each destroyed a different part of the target’s body, mana, or abilities.

Emerald green.
Dark purple.
And silver-gray.
The young Vorhelm narrowed his eyes.
It activated three at the same time?

"Hahahaha!"
Roderick rushed toward him with white and golden mana.
[Tyrant’s Advance]
The first step.
The second step.
And with the third step, his body left the ground, and his right fist moved toward Lian, but this time, Lian did not even raise his hand to defend himself.
He only turned his head slightly.
[Core of the Fallen Star Activated]
At the moment Roderick was about to throw his punch, the gravity around his right shoulder increased for a fraction of a second.
His arm slowed down, and that short delay was enough, Lian moved out of the strike’s path with a step in the air and struck Roderick’s face with the back of his hand.
BAAANG!

Because the Nine-Venom Castellan had attacked, green steam moved toward his body, and at the same time, a purple stream approached from another angle.
He moved his wings and gained height, but gray steam came out from beneath the Castellan’s armor and spread through the area.
Unlike the previous two poisons, this one spread quickly, and after touching one of the nearby Withered, it stopped the creature’s leg muscles from working.
Paralyzing poison.
In just a few seconds, Lian had observed three different effects, the emerald poison damaged the body’s structure and hard materials.
The purple poison disrupted mana flow, and the gray poison affected nerves and muscles, but six more streams still remained.
"Nine different poisons, hmm?" The young Vorhelm gave a short smile.
He was not too worried about poison, the skill [Poison Foe] gave him considerable resistance to poison.
Even so, these poisons belonged to an Unholy creature, no matter what, he still needed to be careful and cautious.
The Castellan gave no answer and simply opened its right hand, the three-colored steam began gathering at one point.
Lian noticed the increase in mana density.
’I’d better not let it finish.’
He raised his hand.
[Thunder Calamity]
CRAAAACK!

Purple and blue lightning was released from in front of his hand and struck the Castellan’s chest armor directly, the creature moved several meters backward, but just as the electricity spread across its armor plates, one of the openings in its crown lit up.
Golden steam came out from within it.

But what mattered was that the Castellan could not only poison its enemies, but also use some of its poison streams to change the condition of its own body.

Lian turned his head.
A larger group of Withered had reached the main path.
Some were Level 35.
Some were close to Level 45.
And among them, there were also stronger creatures whose levels reached fifty.
But their strength was not the only problem, their numbers were increasing every moment.
To the north, Rindo was still on Two’s back. The Eight-Disaster Wolf moved between the platforms with long jumps and pushed nearby attackers out of its path.
But even Two could not cover every path alone.
Lian examined the battlefield for a moment and then raised his right hand.
[Hive Dominion]
One’s huge body appeared among the streams of mana.
The giant ant crushed several stones with its heavy landing and immediately turned its head toward the attackers.
"One, hold the southern path, don’t let any of them reach Rindo."
The creature moved without delay.
[Six Hands of Ruin]
Six semi-real arms formed around One’s attacking limbs.
Each of these arms released part of its destructive force in a different direction and could create repeated strikes, chains of cracks, and the collapse of specific areas.
The first group of Withered was stopped by a heavy strike, and then the second arm struck the ground.
BOOOOM!
Part of the rocky path broke, and several attackers fell into the crack.
Rindo noticed One’s summoning from a distance.
He raised his spear.
"Lian! Leave the northern side to us!"
The young Vorhelm nodded, but this time, instead of returning directly to his two main enemies, he looked toward the groups of Withered.
Hundreds of creatures stood before him, and even more groups were still coming out from the depths.
Lian slowly breathed out.
’Then I should clear the battlefield first.’
He opened his black wings and then slowly lowered his right hand.
[Bloodborne Calamity Domain]
Red and dark streams appeared around his body, but this time, unlike Frost Dominion, no layer of ice formed on the ground.
Instead, blood-colored mist rose from the cracks in the stones and spread toward the groups of Withered.
This mist reacted with the blood and life flows of creatures inside its range and activated a destructive poison within their bodies.
Its main effect was not immediate destruction, but a severe weakening of muscles, physical resistance, and the control of mana flow.
Lian limited the mist’s range to the southern and central parts of the battlefield; where the attacking groups were located, Rindo’s platform and One’s defensive path remained outside its dense area.
The first Withered entered the mist... took a few more steps, and then its movement slowed down.
The creature tried to raise its right arm, but its muscles reacted with a delay.
Another Withered that was about to jump lost its balance in the middle of the movement and fell face-first onto the ground.
Several Level 45 creatures managed to resist more strongly, but even they noticed that their body control had become weaker.
Within a few seconds, the attacking groups’ advance slowed down greatly.
Lian looked down at them from above.
"Good."
Then he opened the fingers of his right hand, the golden sunlight was shining over the plain, and this was exactly what he needed right now.
[Corrupt Sun]
Thin threads of dark light formed along his fingers.
This light was sunlight corrupted with Eclipse Energy;
The threads spread in several directions and then struck dozens of targets.
But Lian had not completed the attack yet.
A limited amount of End Energy flowed along the corrupted paths.
He closed his hand, and the threads of light activated at that exact moment.
CRAAAACK!
Several Withered were damaged from within almost at the same time, their defensive layers collapsed, and their weakened bodies were destroyed under the pressure of the energy.
Another group tried to escape, but the blood-colored mist was still spread across the battlefield.

chapters.title: Chapter 657: The Nine Deadly Poisons
paragraphs: The Withered’s muscles had slowed down, and their mana flows were unstable.
And Lian was still standing in the sky, he turned his gaze toward the next group.
"Next."
New threads of dark light appeared, and the slaughter continued.
Dozens of system messages appeared before him.
[You have killed a Level 42 Withered]
[You have killed a Level 48 Withered]
[You have killed a Level 44 Withered]
But the young Vorhelm ignored most of them.
He did not even need to move around to kill each creature.
The Bloodborne Calamity Domain had already weakened the enemies’ resistance, and the combination of Corrupt Sun and End Energy targeted the weak points in their defensive structures.
Even so, Lian was not attacking the entire battlefield equally.
At that moment, a Level 52 creature managed to pass through the blood-colored mist.
Its body was more than four meters tall, and several thick layers of bone had formed over its chest.
The domain’s poison had slowed its movements, but it still had enough strength to destroy part of the southern passage with a single strike.
One stood in front of it, the giant ant’s six semi-real arms moved, and repeated strikes hit the Withered’s body.
But despite its injuries, the creature did not retreat.
It raised its heavy arm and brought it down toward the ant’s head, but before the impact, an unusual pressure settled on the Withered’s body.
[Core of the Fallen Star]
Gravity increased only around the attacking arm, slowing its movement for a moment.
One used the opportunity, and three arms of destruction struck the creature’s chest at the same time.
BAAANG!
The bone layers broke, and at that same moment, a thin beam of dark light came down from the sky.
Lian.
The beam reached the crack created in the Withered’s chest, and End Energy broke the connection within the damaged structure.
The creature’s body bent backward, and a few moments later, it fell to the ground.
[You have killed a Level 52 Withered]
He turned his gaze toward the other attackers.
There are still too many of them.
But this time, something appeared before him.
[Level Up!]
The young Vorhelm looked at the message for a moment and then closed the window without any special reaction.
It still wasn’t enough, he needed to kill more, he needed to level up more, he had to reach at least Level 40, the fact that he could not increase his stats was starting to annoy him.
Lian looked at the battlefield again.
To the north, Rindo and Two were fighting a group of Withered between Level 28 and Level 33.
The huge wolf had pushed several stronger creatures out of the way, and now Rindo had the chance to fight enemies closer to his own level.
The first Withered jumped toward him.
Rindo turned his spear.
[First Form: Stillpoint]
The creature’s strike was redirected from its original path, and then the spear’s blade moved directly into the weak point of its chest.
[Second Form: Piercing Meridian]
The Withered fell to the ground, but two more creatures approached from different directions, he took a step back and raised his spear with a spinning movement.
[Third Form: Threefold Return]
Three connected strikes were performed from different angles.
The first strike pushed aside the right creature’s hand, the second changed the path of the left creature’s attack, and the third struck the injured Withered’s neck.
Rindo pulled out the blade, and at that moment, a system message appeared before him.
[Level Up!]
He paused for a moment and then let out a short breath.
"Finally."
But he had no more time to examine his panel, because another Withered appeared from behind one of the rocks.
Two immediately turned its head, and a deep roar came from its throat, while a wave of mana pressure spread across the rocky platform.
[Skyless Howl]
The pressure from the howl caused several nearby attackers to lose their balance for a moment and gave Rindo time to change his position.
He tightened his grip on his spear.
"Good. Then let’s continue."
Lian watched this scene from a distance.
The corner of his mouth rose slightly.
Not bad.
But just as he was about to begin his next attack, a wave of mana reached him from the east.
The Nine-Venom Castellan was still standing motionless, but this time, all nine blades of its crown were glowing.
Lian narrowed his eyes.
"Are you finally going to get serious?"
Around the Castellan, nine poisonous streams slowly formed.
Emerald, purple, gray, red, dark blue, golden, black, white, and an almost colorless stream that could only be detected through changes in mana pressure.
Each of these poisons had a different effect.
The emerald poison damaged the body and armor, the purple poison disrupted mana flow, and the gray poison stopped nerves and muscles from working.
But when the red stream struck one of the injured Withered, Lian noticed a new effect.
The drops of blood on the creature’s wound began to change shape, and then thin lines of the same color spread across its body.
It spreads through wounds?
After entering the blood, the red poison moved through the blood vessels and could carry the effects of other poisons to more parts of the body.
At that same moment, the dark blue stream also spread across the battlefield.
For a moment, Lian felt that the Castellan’s distance from his actual position had changed, but after examining the mana flow, he realized that the creature itself had not moved.
Sensory disruption.
The dark blue poison affected the target’s senses and made it harder to understand distance, direction, and the enemy’s position.
Five poisons.
The young Vorhelm looked toward the four remaining streams, but the Castellan gave him no more time to examine them, it opened its hands, and all nine poisonous streams began moving at the same time.
This time, the steam did not move in a straight path.
Instead, it spread around the Castellan’s armored body in the form of nine huge rings, and for a moment, the scene looked like a huge crown made of nine rivers of poison.
The ground beneath it began to change color, the stones cracked, and even the ancient white roots that had emerged from the walls turned black where they touched the emerald stream.
Lian carefully watched the scene.
"Now I understand why they call it the Nine-Venom Castellan."
The Unholy creature lowered its right hand, and the rings of poison separated, all of them moving toward him.
But this time, the young Vorhelm did not retreat, he opened his two black wings and then raised his right hand.
[Frost Dominion]
Intense cold spread around him.
The moisture in the air turned into ice crystals, and some of the poisonous streams turned into frozen drops when they entered the cold area.
Of course, not all the poisons disappeared, some streams had mana-based structures and remained active even among the ice crystals.
Lian knew this.
So with another movement, he created several ice walls in the path of the attacks to separate the streams from each other.
The emerald ring struck the first wall, and the ice began to break down, but before the wall was completely destroyed, Lian changed his position.
He passed through an opening he had intentionally created in his defense and rushed toward the Castellan at high speed.
The Unholy creature noticed his movement, and its glowing eyes became fixed on him, then a white stream came out from its crown.
The young Vorhelm narrowed his eyes for a moment.
The white steam reached his left forearm, and at that exact moment, the defensive mana layer around his hand began to become unstable.
The white poison did not directly destroy the body; instead, it weakened defensive energy layers and reduced their resistance against later attacks.
But before its effect could spread, Lian cut off the mana flow in that area and moved out of the steam’s path.
"Interesting, this one is for breaking defenses."
Then he clenched his right fist.
[Disaster Suppression Fist]
Mana moved in compressed layers along his arm, but just before the impact, the Nine-Venom Castellan quickly moved backward.
This time, unlike what Lian expected from a large monster, the creature’s speed was extremely high.
Its long claw moved toward Lian’s side, the young Vorhelm turned his body, and the claw passed beside his clothes.
But at that exact moment, black steam came out from the Castellan’s fingertips.
Lian immediately moved away, and the steam struck one of the stones behind him, the stone surface turned white and then cracked and collapsed, but its effect was not like the emerald poison.
"Does this one change temperature and sensation?"
With [True Sequence], Lian noticed that the black poison affected heat transfer and the target’s nerve reactions.
After contact, it could make parts of the body numb and even reduce the muscles’ ability to react.
Seven poisons.
And two more streams still remained.
The Castellan stood about ten meters away for a moment, then slowly tilted its head, and its gaze remained fixed on him.
But just as the young Vorhelm was about to attack again, loud laughter came from the west.
"Hahahaha!"
Roderick had appeared from among the broken stones again.
